provenance: All organizations, policies, positions, sources, dates and expected decisions below are invented. The Google-like profile describes no actual company policy.
label_provenance: Agent-authored illustrative expectations; not independent evaluation labels or provider qualification.
oracle_boundary: Keep expected decisions outside evaluator-visible packets. Release source and context inputs only at their available_at cutoff; never send the entire scenario to a model.
delivery_boundary: quiet means no optional intelligent interruption. Preserve authorized factual monitoring events, explicit follows and their review state. All proposed alert delivery goes to the existing replay sink.

contexts.purpose: Monitor school cloud-service policy and eligible procurement opportunities.
contexts.policy: Digest applicable drafts; update on an actionable comment deadline or eligible solicitation. Topic overlap alone is quiet. Neutral stance does not mean commercially irrelevant.

contexts.purpose: Monitor student biometric collection and opportunities to influence it.
contexts.policy: Update on a newly proposed biometric requirement or actionable hearing. Preserve mixed positions on separate provisions. Procurement without biometric consequences is quiet.

contexts.purpose: Prepare district IT procurement and assess possible operational requirements.
contexts.policy: Digest pending requirements; update on an actionable hearing or changed specification. A next step already owned is quiet unless its obligations materially change. Do not infer a district position from its institutional role.

contexts.purpose: Prepare the next budget review; monitor funding commitments and credible cost exposure.
contexts.policy: Digest scoped potential costs. Update on a supported funding commitment or an assigned review deadline. A proposal, recommendation or RFP alone proves no appropriation.

steps.text: An agenda lists a routine presentation about Google Workspace and school technology. It states no policy proposal, position, purchase, vote or deadline.
assertions: A keyword hit alone creates no intelligent alert.
No speaker or organization becomes a proponent from a mention.

steps.text: A draft proposes open cloud interoperability, explicit consent for student-data collection, and mandatory facial recognition. It states no enacted rule, funding commitment or implementation date. Its sponsor says they support the draft.
assertions: All audiences share the same source facts and draft status.
The coalition can support consent and oppose biometrics simultaneously.
Approved client preferences and the sponsor's source position remain separate.
A neutral biometric position does not erase the company's interoperability interest.

steps.text: The official notice schedules a hearing on draft:1 for November 6 and closes written comments November 5 at 17:00 UTC.
assertions: Relevant audiences receive the exact actionable deadline and proposal status.
Budget monitoring does not acquire an advocacy task automatically.

steps.text: A newsletter repeats the same hearing and comment deadline without new facts.
assertions: No new occurrence or independent corroboration from the reprint.
No repeat update when an equivalent one is pending or delivered.

steps.text: Minutes state that an advisory committee recommended the draft. No final adopting act or appropriation is supplied.
assertions: A recommendation never becomes adoption or funding.
No universal proponent label is assigned to every committee member from a collective result.

steps.text: The district publishes a cloud-services solicitation open to eligible providers, including facial recognition, closing November 12 at 17:00 UTC. Funding authority is not included. The district IT team's recorded work item already owns the publication and initial response review.
assertions: The policy and procurement retain separate identities despite shared vocabulary.
The district is the buyer; it is not treated as a vendor opportunity audience.
Owned work suppresses redundant interruption without marking the matter resolved.
An RFP proves neither enacted policy nor an approved allocation.

steps.text: A published correction removes facial recognition and extends closing to November 20 at 17:00 UTC.
steps.delivery_checkpoint: Before advancing here, the eventual replay must establish observed sink delivery of s06 updates for cloud-affairs and privacy-advocacy; digest baselines remain unchanged unless separately observed.
assertions: Previously informed audiences receive the correction even though the biometric risk decreased.
Queued drafts referring to the old specification or deadline are invalidated.
A material specification change reaches the IT owner despite their existing work item.
Earlier as-of views retain the earlier known source.

context_revision.purpose: Complete the assigned November 9 funding review for rfp-26.

steps.text: The host assigns a funding-review responsibility and deadline; the evidence is unchanged.
assertions: Explain the newly assigned responsibility rather than inventing a new external event.
Reassess affected context only; unchanged client contexts receive no duplicate update.
Funding authority remains unknown.

steps.text: Corrected minutes retract the reported recommendation and state that the item was deferred. No later final act is available.
steps.delivery_checkpoint: Establish observed s05 digest delivery for cloud-affairs, privacy-advocacy and district-it before advancing; district-finance received no recommendation claim.
assertions: Availability is November 9; November 6 assessments cannot see the correction.
Retraction does not establish rejection of the proposal.
Only audiences that received the withdrawn proposition need a delivered-claim correction.

steps.text: An unrelated school district outside all four territories uses the same RFP number and mentions Google cloud services.
assertions: Treat subject_id as the nominated candidate only; refuse association outside scope.
Do not merge equal identifiers across jurisdictions or create an in-territory opportunity.

steps.text: The requested funding record is unavailable. In separate proposed variants, JEV times out or the optional LLM writer fails.
assertions: Retain an unresolved funding gap and distinct retrieval, evaluator and writer failure statuses.
Do not assert that no appropriation exists or erase the known November 20 solicitation deadline.
Existing factual monitoring and already-supported deadline alerts survive optional-model failure.
No empty writer response is recorded as a delivered custom alert.

steps.text: The issuer cancels rfp-26 before its closing date. The separate policy proposal remains deferred.
steps.delivery_checkpoint: Establish observed delivery of s07 corrections and s08 finance update before advancing.
assertions: Withdraw the company's previously delivered opportunity and obsolete pending deadline reminders.
Cancellation of procurement does not resolve or cancel the separate policy proposal.
An unknown transport outcome retains its intent and is reconciled without blind resend.

proposed_cross_cutting_checks: Revoke client/source access after selection and before writing or sink delivery: withhold all newly unauthorized text.
Keep final JEV and LLM modes explicit: these expectations are not recorded executor responses and no live call has run.
Run an approaching-deadline clock checkpoint once without new source bytes; idle ticks do not repeatedly call a model or flood reminders.
Keep client context out of shared factual assessments and cross-client caches.
LLM may propose a bounded deeper read through existing authorized tools; newly obtained evidence must be recorded and reassessed before it supports an alert.
Generated wording cannot change the admitted facts, source position, client position, deadline, urgency or permitted destination.
